## DemoTransVoice v0.1.3

This release fixes the ways a working setup could look broken: the playback thread could die and keep the microphone muted forever, a bad device name aborted startup while leaving every worker thread behind, the language prefix the model streams ahead of the transcript was read out loud, and batch transcription dropped whole utterances on a three-second read timeout. The sentence splitter also stopped turning the spaces between English words into Chinese commas.

CPU note: nothing here needs a GPU. The two llama-server containers from v0.1.2 are unchanged.

## Fixes

### A failed output device no longer mutes the microphone for good

`AudioPlayer._run` set `_playing = True` and *then* opened the output stream, with the open outside the `try`. A device that refused to open (wrong name, unsupported rate, a Bluetooth headset switching profiles) killed the playback thread while `_playing` stayed `True`. In 外放 mode (`mute_during_tts`) the gate waits for `is_playing` to become false, so the microphone stayed closed for the rest of the session: the pipeline looked alive, heard nothing, and said nothing. The device is opened before the flag is raised, the flag is cleared in a `finally`, and a stream error no longer leaves the player in a "playing" state.

### Startup failures unwind instead of leaking

`Pipeline.run` started the player, the TTS pool, the ASR worker and two loops *before* opening the capture stream, and that open sat outside the `try`. A device name that matched nothing raised `ValueError` straight out of `run()` — no `shutdown()`, so every thread and both HTTP client pools stayed alive while the GUI showed "已停止". The microphone is now acquired first, inside an `ExitStack`, and every exit path (error, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>, normal stop) funnels through `shutdown()`. `MicCapture` also closes its stream when `start()` fails, instead of leaving the handle allocated.

### Device settings accept a number again

`--mic-device 3` / `--output-device 3` were documented as "index or name" but handled as a name only, so a plain number was searched for as a substring of device names (matching whichever device happened to contain it) and failed if none did. A purely numeric value — with an optional sign and surrounding spaces — is now used as the PortAudio index; anything else stays a case- and space-insensitive name fragment.

### The language prefix is no longer spoken

With streaming ASR and no `language` set, llama-server streams its bookkeeping line token by token: `lang`, `language Chi`, `language Chinese<asr_text>`, then the transcript. The first delta used to be published immediately, so "language" reached the TTS queue — and because the pipeline advanced its cursor to that length, the first real characters were then dropped by `text[pushed:]`. The prefix is now *gated*: a window publishes nothing while its accumulated text can still turn into that line, and is settled (stripped or passed through) as soon as the marker arrives or the shape is ruled out. The pattern that strips it is case-insensitive, matching the gate.

### Batch transcription is no longer cut off after three seconds

`READ_TIMEOUT_S = 3.0` was applied to whole-segment requests too. A batch request has no intermediate output — the server is silent for the entire decode — so every non-trivial utterance timed out, was published as empty text, and its audio was dropped with one line on stderr. Batch requests now use their own 60 s read timeout; streaming keeps the short one, where silence really does mean a stalled window.

### Punctuation

`normalize_punct` turned every whitespace run into `，`, which is right for a CJK clause break and wrong between English words: `hello world` became `hello，world` and the TTS read a comma in the middle of it. A space is now kept as a space when either neighbour is an ASCII letter or digit, and only becomes a comma where both sides are non-Latin.

## Tests

`tests/` is new and covers the segmenter (`test_segmenter.py`) — the splitting rules that used to be verified by reading. Run it with `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest`.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `DemoTransVoice-0.1.3-win-x64.zip` | x64 build of `DemoTransVoice-gui.exe` and `DemoTransVoice.exe` with `config.ini` and `speaker.wav` beside them — the ASR and TTS servers are still yours to run |

## Notes

- Windows x64. `config.ini` is read from the folder that holds the executables, so the zip can be unpacked anywhere and edited in place; a `config.ini` already present is never overwritten by a rebuild.
- The defaults expect an ASR server at `127.0.0.1:45101` and a TTS server at `127.0.0.1:45102` (see `config.ini` and `Dockerfile.tts`). `silence_threshold` is machine-specific: the startup banner prints the measured ambient RMS, and the GUI status bar shows 有声 / 静默 against the running threshold.
- Unchanged from v0.1.2: the pause-driven model (one `sentence_gap_ms` for sentence boundaries, one `utterance_gap_ms` for the end of a segment), the ring buffer with backlog retry, and the `mute_during_tts` gate.
- Stack: Python 3.11+ · numpy · sounddevice · soundfile · httpx · tkinter control panel with a Win32 tray icon · PyInstaller one-dir build.
